canonical.detail: State the real spaces, load, sign convention, mesh, conforming RT0/P1 trial family, and squared residual functional; the proof suppliers establish conformity and norm equivalence separately.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Ultraweak Poisson DPG spaces and plan-consistent bilinear form
canonical.detail: Define each skeleton trace as a range quotient with its extension infimum; write all orientation and sign conventions explicitly. The local quotient/gluing theorem justifies well-definedness and completeness.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Least-squares residual norm is equivalent to H(div) x H1_0 error
canonical.detail: Use the H^1_0 density definition to establish the weak Green identity, pair the first residual with grad(delta u), apply bounded-domain Poincare, and recover both graph components; prove the reverse estimate by triangle inequalities.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Exact local finite Riesz solves for practical DPG tests
canonical.detail: Specify inputs, exact output tests, element-local Gram systems, an exact positive-definiteness check, and the failure status; numerical quadrature and floating solve errors are not included.

canonical.name: Local dual trace lifting by a scalar H1 Riesz solve
canonical.detail: Represent a scalar trace-dual functional on H1 by Riesz; its vanishing on H1_0 forces the Riesz vector to solve Delta z=z distributionally, so grad z is H(div) and its weak normal trace is the original functional.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Ultraweak Poisson skeleton spaces are Hilbert trace quotients
canonical.detail: Prove trace-map continuity and closed kernels, identify range norms with quotient norms, and prove the scalar and normal-trace gluing implications by elementwise Green identities and facet cancellation.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Exact DPG stability does not certify quadrature or algebraic solve errors
canonical.detail: State the exact-analysis boundary and quote only the literal normal-equation condition-number theorem; no numerical stability claim is inferred.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: The ultraweak Poisson DPG bilinear form is bounded
canonical.detail: For each skeleton pairing choose an admissible global or broken lift, apply the local Green-dual trace bound, take the extension infimum, and combine the five terms by Cauchy-Schwarz.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: The ultraweak Poisson trial operator has trivial kernel
canonical.detail: Test first with compactly supported element fields to derive the distributional first-order and divergence equations, identify the skeleton traces by Green duality, glue to H^1_0 and H(div), then test the homogeneous weak Poisson solution with itself.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: The RT0/P1 least-squares family is conforming
canonical.detail: Use the actual RT0 facet-flux unisolvence/conformity supplier for the flux and the global H^1_0 definition for the continuous piecewise P1 component; finite mesh polynomial spaces are finite dimensional.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: A uniformly bounded Fortin map for the practical P1/R3 DPG family
canonical.detail: Construct the scalar moment projector and RT2 subspace moment projector explicitly for p=1,d=2; prove the full RT2 unisolvence needed by the moment system, all four DPG moment identities, and shape-uniform reference-to-cell graph bounds.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Ideal Poisson DPG trial-to-test Riesz map
canonical.detail: Specify the bounded functional on the real Hilbert test space, invoke the exact published Riesz hypotheses, and define the ideal test space without claiming its computability.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: The conforming RT0/P1 least-squares Poisson minimizer is unique and best approximating
canonical.detail: Use the actual weak Poisson existence supplier under its Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice hypotheses, identify the least-squares residual with the linear residual map of the error, and use finite-dimensional orthogonal projection in the equivalent residual inner product.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: A topology-free bounded lifting of every ultraweak Poisson load
canonical.detail: Represent an arbitrary broken graph-dual load by its four exact Riesz coefficients, solve one global H1_0 problem, form a global H(div) field with the required divergence, use actual global traces, verify all five signed pairings, and prove a mesh-independent product-norm bound.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Adjoint graph inf-sup for ultraweak Poisson on connected Lipschitz polyhedra
canonical.detail: Prove the connected-domain graph bounds from the bounded arbitrary-load right inverse and the zero trial kernel; the global construction has no simple-connectivity or connected-boundary hypothesis and is uniform over the stated mesh family.
canonical.historical_authoring_disposition: The current complete Poisson DPG source route proves the adjoint graph inf-sup after a global Hodge decomposition under simple connectivity. Preserve the approved connected Lipschitz scope; a complete topology-corrected local proof is still required before readiness.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Ideal ultraweak Poisson DPG is the energy best approximation
canonical.detail: The trivial trial kernel makes the Riesz trial-to-test map injective; its image inner product is the energy inner product, and finite-dimensional orthogonal projection gives existence, uniqueness, best approximation, and the residual identity.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Fortin stability and quasi-optimality for practical DPG
canonical.detail: Derive the discrete inf-sup bound from the explicit Fortin identities, express the practical DPG equations as the mixed residual Riesz system, apply the exact Babuška–Brezzi supplier, and prove the quasi-optimal estimate.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: Practical DPG residual is reliable and efficient up to data oscillation
canonical.detail: Prove the full residual-representer reliability identity by orthogonal projection onto the discrete test space, use the Fortin property to bound the omitted component, derive efficiency from restriction of the full dual norm, and identify the Poisson data oscillation.

canonical.name: Batch-local result: P1/R3 practical DPG quasi-optimality and residual estimator for Poisson
canonical.detail: Instantiate the continuous graph theorem only in the dimension-two triangular P1/R3 family selected in PE30; retain all connected Lipschitz polygons including holes and the exact cell-average data-oscillation estimate.
canonical.historical_authoring_disposition: Instantiate the generic Fortin and residual theorems with p=1,d=2, use mean-preserving scalar moments to obtain the cell-average oscillation bound, and retain the connected-domain graph inf-sup proof obligation explicitly.
